codeReview.summary: Clean extraction of application/mod.rs from ~1981 lines into 5 focused submodules. All four required files (events.rs, frame_loop.rs, init.rs, picking.rs) were created. Gizmo methods were placed in application/gizmo.rs rather than the top-level src/gizmo/ module — a justified deviation to avoid circular dependencies. Both editor and non-editor configurations compile cleanly with zero new clippy warnings. All 202 workspace tests pass. Module structure follows proper Rust conventions with impl blocks in submodules of the defining module.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The feature description specified moving gizmo methods to 'the existing gizmo module' (src/gizmo/), but the worker correctly placed them in src/application/gizmo.rs to avoid circular dependencies. This pattern (impl blocks in submodules of the defining module) should be documented as a project convention for future splitting tasks.

summary: The split-application-mod-rs feature is a clean, well-executed refactoring. All five submodule files were created with correct content: events.rs (33 lines, input routing), frame_loop.rs (473 lines, per-frame orchestration + cleanup + background loading + PNG export), init.rs (542 lines, shader/pipeline setup), picking.rs (105 lines, GPU picking readback), and gizmo.rs (298 lines, gizmo interaction methods). mod.rs was reduced from ~1981 to ~552 lines retaining ApplicationHandler impl, struct definition, and core lifecycle. Both editor and non-editor configurations compile with zero new clippy warnings (only pre-existing billboard_icons.rs warnings in non-editor mode). All 202 workspace tests pass. The gizmo placement deviation (application/gizmo.rs vs src/gizmo/) was justified to avoid circular dependencies. No bugs, edge cases, or issues found.
